cards.text: The Teacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem (Ecclesiastes 1:1), is still handing out wisdom one short saying at a time. He's just been talking about fools, kings and leaky roofs (Ecclesiastes 10). Now he opens with this: “Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again.”
Next, the Teacher says to divide your portion among seven, or even eight. SEVEN wasn't enough, so this man just rounds UP.

cards.question: Why does the Teacher say to divide your portion among seven or even eight?

answers.text: You don't know what disaster may come
Whatever you keep will spoil anyway
Sharing will bring you honor in the city

cards.text: Never put all your chocolate chips in one cookie, friend. Then the Teacher looks at the sky: if the clouds are full, they pour out rain upon the earth.

cards.question: The Teacher says a tree may fall to the south or to the north. Where does he say it lies?

answers.text: Right in the place where it falls

cards.text: Now the Teacher pictures someone out in the field who just stands there watching the wind. Just… watching.

cards.question: The Teacher says the one who keeps watching the wind will fail to ___.
The Teacher also says the one who keeps watching the clouds will fail to reap.

cards.text: That's checking the weather app TWELVE times and never leaving the house. Then the Teacher names two things you don't know: the path of the wind, and how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb.

cards.question: You don't know the path of the wind or how bones form in the womb. So what does the Teacher say you cannot understand?
The Teacher calls God the Maker of all things.

cards.text: Back to the field: sow your seed in the morning, and don't rest your hands in the evening. Morning shift AND evening shift, friend, that's my whole bakery schedule, and I've never been happier.

cards.question: The Teacher says to keep sowing morning and evening, because you do not know which will ___.
The Teacher says only one of the sowings can prosper, never both.

cards.text: Then the Teacher says, “Light is sweet, and it pleases the eyes to see the sun.” Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and you do NOT have to tell me twice.

cards.question: If a man lives many years, what does the Teacher tell him to do with them?
Rejoice in all those years, the Teacher says, but remember the days of ___.
The Teacher says the days of darkness will be few.

cards.text: And he ends right here: “Everything to come is futile.” Friend, I've got sprinkles for just about everything, but that line I'm leaving exactly how he said it.

findings.problem: The question types fall into a repeating rhythm. Every cluster of choice cards ends with a true or false follow-up on the same verse, right after another choice card: cards 7–8, 10–11, 13–14 and 17–18. Cards 7–8 and 13–14 are both a fill in the blank followed by a true or false. Within a stop, this is a pattern, not a natural choice for each card.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: Verse 1 is the passage's key opening picture, "Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again." Card 1 only quotes it. No card unpacks what the picture means, and no choice card asks about it. For a wisdom passage, this leaves the baker without the meaning of its central image.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: Card 19 says "And he ends right here," but the Teacher doesn't end at 11:8. He keeps going in 11:9. This passage ends there, the Teacher doesn't, so the line points out something that isn't true.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.
